text:
Marathon Petroleum rose slightly today on a backdrop of sharp gains over the past two weeks, driven primarily by the escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Iran's attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats of further retaliation have pushed crude oil prices sharply higher—Brent crude touched $110 this week—and refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with moderate inventory levels, a combination that typically strengthens refiner margins (the profit spread between crude input costs and finished fuel sales).

The two-week rally reflects both the tighter supply outlook from Middle East disruption risk and the surge in tanker costs, which has pushed the real delivery cost of physical oil well above the spot price. For a large U.S. refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices and constrained global supply can improve profitability on existing inventory and future production, even as they raise input costs.
